title: Async Services & Application State
objectives: Share application state across handlers safely

examples.name: state.rs

exercise.prompt: Classify async hazards: "std::fs::read in an async handler" (blocks executor), "Arc<Mutex<DB pool>>" (fine — short locks), "tokio::task::spawn per request unbounded" (unbounded task creation), "await inside a lock guard" (deadlock risk).
hints: Blocking the executor starves every task on that worker thread.
Locks must stay short and never span an await.

questions.prompt: Why must async handlers avoid std::fs::read on large files?
options: it blocks the executor thread, stalling every task on it
questions.explanation: Use tokio::fs (or spawn_blocking) so the executor keeps serving other requests.

questions.prompt: Application state (db pool, config) is typically shared via…
options: Arc-wrapped state passed to handlers by the framework
questions.explanation: Arc-shared state injected by the router is idiomatic and testable.
